newsitem.title: UK: Applied Distribution downbeat on H2 trade.
newsitem.headline: Applied Distribution downbeat on H2 trade.

text.p: Applied Distribution Group Plc said on Thursday that its trading performance has deteriorated and that it will trade at break-even in the second half.
The company said it has been experiencing specific problems and incurring losses on certain contracts, which it started in the second half of 1995.
Applied Distribution said that it has decided not to recommend any final dividend payment.

"In view of these revised expectations for 1996 the board considers that it would be prudent to rebase dividends in line with the anticipated lower level of sustainable profitability," said the company in a statement.
Shares in the company had plunged 29p to 33-1/2p by 0839 GMT on the back of the announcement.

Applied Distribution said that without significant new business gains to replace expiring contracts it is unlikely to achieve a level of operating profits in 1997 "which will be materially better than in 1996."
However, it said that it exepcts an improvement during 1997 from current trading levels as losses are eliminated and as management actions taken to improve profitability take hold.

The company made pre-tax profits of 5.07 million stg for the year ending December 31, 1995. Its latest results showed that profits in the six months ended June 29 tumbled to 240,000 stg from 2.23 million previously.
